text:
Aria N: Quick heads-up: several of our samples and one internal CLI started failing after the exports cleanup in 3.3.0. Symptoms vary across runtimes (pnpm workspace, vite dev prebundle, and Cloudflare Worker builds).

Ben C: What errors are you seeing?

Aria N: Example errors: 
- node (pnpm workspace): Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports"
- vite dev: Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/sdk-js/dist/index.js' does not provide an export named 'default'
- cloudflare wrangler build: Module "@redwood/sdk-js" resolves to ESM but downstream code does a require -> runtime crash.

Roshi P: Which exact exports did we publish? Did anyone remove the package.json subpath or wildcard order? Some bundlers rely on the ./package.json entry to read metadata at prebundle time.

Aria N: Published exports snippet from node_modules on a repro machine: {".": {"import":"./esm/index.mjs","types":"./types/index.d.ts"},"./*":"./*"} — no ./package.json subpath, no require conditional.

Ben C: Ok that explains pnpm/workspace tooling and some bundlers. pnpm / esbuild / vite sometimes import package.json subpath during optimization. Also removing a CJS require branch breaks consumers that still do const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk-js') or import default.

Roshi P: Two parts to immediate fix: 1) re-add the ./package.json export so tools can statically inspect package metadata; 2) add a conditional require branch so require() resolves to a CJS build while import uses ESM. That keeps edge runtimes happy and restores legacy consumer behavior.

CI Bot: CI noticed failing sample jobs referencing samples/monorepo-playground and samples/worker-proxy since 3.3.0 publish. Failing builds: vite-prebundle-smoke, pnpm-workspace-install. See https://ci.redwood/exports/1456

Aria N: Also TypeScript issues: tsc in some consumer repos throws "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk-js'" or complains no default export. We need a d.ts shim that provides both export = and export default shapes.

Ben C: For typings we can add a lightweight index.d.ts at root that does: declare const SDK: any; export = SDK; export default SDK; That is ugly but prevents mass breakage. Longer term we should publish proper named exports.

Roshi P: Another nuance: the wildcard export order matters for some resolvers. If ./* appears before '.' in the exports object, some tools will match subpaths in surprising ways. Double-check the published order.

Aria N: Good call — on the published package the wildcard was after '.', but a packaging step in CI accidentally reorders keys. I'll include a strict script that validates the final tarball exports map before publish.

Docs Team: We should also add a short migration note in SDK docs explaining safe import patterns and a compatibility section listing known pitfalls (pnpm, vite prebundle, Cloudflare Workers, electron).

Ben C: Proposed rollout: patch PR that (A) restores "./package.json" export, (B) adds "require" -> ./cjs/index.cjs conditional, (C) bundles a d.ts shim for default/export= interop, (D) adds a prepublish verification to ensure exports keys are stable. Publish as canary tag `canary/exports-compat` and run the failing sample CI jobs.

Roshi P: Also add CI smoke jobs: pnpm workspace install + vite optimizeDeps + wrangler build. Include Node 12/14/16/18 matrix to catch CJS/ESM loader differences.

CI Bot: Patch PR queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/629. Canary publish job cb-canary-629 queued.

Aria N: I'll open a small repro repo for maintainers to quickly validate. Will link PR and ping once canary is live. Thanks for the quick triage.

Ben C: Thanks. After canary passes we should message #devex and customer-success with recommended pins and a timeline for stricter exports in a future major.

Roshi P: Agreed. Also add a contributor checklist for export map changes so this doesn't regress again.

Docs Team: Noted — will add a short guide and migration snippet to docs/sdk/migration-exports.md once the patch lands.
